verses.text: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.
Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go yonder. We will worship, and come back to you.”
Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.
Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am, my son.” He said, “Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.
They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.
Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
Yahweh’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”

Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
Abraham called the name of that place Yahweh Will Provide.  As it is said to this day, “On Yahweh’s mountain, it will be provided.”
Yahweh’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,
and said, “I have sworn by myself, says Yahweh, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son,

that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring  greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring  will possess the gate of his enemies.
All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring,  because you have obeyed my voice.”
So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

footnotes.content: I still marvel that the God who calls Abraham 'friend' would test him so severely. Even so, a father's love can be tested, and God Himself knows what it is to give what He loves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The words cut to the quick: 'your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac.' God does not hide the weight of it. Yet in that weight, I see the tenderness of a God who would one day not spare His own Son for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham rose early. There was no delay, no bargaining - only obedience born of trust. I have learned that faith often walks quietly in the dark, moving one step at a time toward what God has said.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three days of walking toward that mountain must have been three days of aching. Yet Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place. Sometimes faith sees the place God has appointed long before it makes sense to our hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What courage of faith to say, 'We will worship, and come back to you.' Abraham clung to God's promise that Isaac would be the heir. I am learning to trust that the God who gives the promise will keep it, even when the path leads through sorrow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wood for the offering was laid on Isaac, the fire and knife in his father's hands. They went together in love. How much more did the Son go willingly, carrying His own wood to Calvary for the love of the Father and for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaac's question is simple and trusting: 'Where is the lamb for a burnt offering?' It pierces an old man's heart. I too have asked that question, and I bless God that the answer came in the Person of Jesus, the Lamb of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham speaks with quiet faith: 'God will provide himself the lamb.' He could not have known all that those words held. But our God did provide Himself in the Lamb, slain from the foundation of the world for sinners like me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The altar was built, the wood laid in order, and Isaac bound. What obedience of love on both sides. I weep to think of it, and yet I rejoice that my Savior was not spared, bound by love for me on a greater altar.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The knife was raised. A father stretched out his hand to do the hardest thing imaginable. At the last moment, God Himself stayed it. And one day, the Father would not stay His hand, but would give His only Son for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How tender that the Lord calls twice: 'Abraham, Abraham.' He knows His servant, and He calls him by name in mercy. I am grateful that our God still calls us by name to turn us from the edge of despair to His provision.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God says, 'Now I know that you fear God.' Not that He learned anything, but that Abraham's faith was proved genuine. True fear of God is not terror alone, but trust that loves Him enough to obey even when it costs everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God provided a ram caught in the thicket. Abraham's eyes were opened to see it. How often the Lord has opened my old eyes to see His provision right behind me, just when I thought all was lost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham called the place Yahweh Will Provide. To this day the name points us to the mountain where our God would provide the true Lamb. On that greater mountain of Calvary, He provided Himself for the salvation of His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel of Yahweh speaks again, a second time. God is not stingy with His grace. After sparing, He speaks blessing again. I take comfort that the God who delivers us also delights to bless us in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God swears by Himself, for there is none greater. When our hope is built on the oath of the God who cannot lie, our faith rests on something unshakeable. How blessed we are that our salvation rests on His oath in Christ Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God promises to multiply Abraham's offspring beyond number, and to give them victory over their enemies. Yet the greatest fulfillment is that from Abraham would come One Offspring who would crush the serpent's head and give us victory over our greatest enemy, sin and death.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the nations of the earth are blessed by Abraham's Offspring. That is the Gospel. Not just Israel, but Gentiles like me, brought near by faith to be blessed in Jesus Christ, the true Seed of Abraham.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham and the young men went together to Beersheba. The father and son were both spared. After the agony of the mountain, there was peace in going home together. One day, all God's children will go home together to the place He has prepared for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After the mountain of sacrifice, the record turns to family lines. God is faithful to generations - He had already been at work providing a wife for Isaac in Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel. Even in ordinary family records, our God is quietly weaving the story of redemption toward Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
